figures.title: Topological propagation through shared logic. Evaluate gate 5 in topological order. Earlier internal values remain available, and an output is computed only after every predecessor value has been determined.

The factored network computes (a+b+c)(d+e)f+g using two wide OR gates, one three-input AND and one final OR. It uses four gates only under this declared wide-gate library. A two-input library requires another mapping.
Cofactors determine mux data pins. Select pair 11 fixes A and B while C takes both values. The ordered pair [0, 1] determines exactly one residual data function, not an arbitrary mux connection.
A shared decoder generates two outputs. Address 7 activates exactly decoder row 7. Parity and majority independently select their output bits, producing stored word 11 in the declared output order.
Polarity-correct NAND mapping. At row 7, the first-stage NAND gates complement AB and AC. The final NAND restores their OR, so both displayed implementations agree on this fully specified row.

Two corresponding output pairs feed separate XOR gates; their discrepancies are ORed into one miter. The drawn example agrees on both outputs. Equivalence requires zero discrepancy for every allowed input, not only this example.

Different extrema for contamination and propagation. For net Y=qD, compute contamination with predecessor minima and propagation with predecessor maxima. These independent structural bounds do not assert that every possible input transition reaches the output.
